personas.name: Maren Okafor
personas.who: 41, Year 5 teacher, 28 in the class. Confident with a browser, no patience for setup. Straight from the research emotionalContext: standing, 8-12 feet from a wall panel, room lights on, roughly six seconds before the room's attention breaks.
personas.context: Wall-mounted 1280x800 touch panel at the front of the room, tapping with one hand while half-facing the class. Lights on, panel washed out. Mid-lesson, no time to troubleshoot.
personas.task: Cold-call eight students fairly for the last ten minutes of a lesson, without picking the same three kids and without any child believing she chose them on purpose.
personas.verdict: She got spins out of it, but she did not finish the job as she meant to. She typed 28 names live in front of the class because there is nowhere to keep a roster, the names on the wheel were unreadable from the second row, the winner appeared in 24px text on a 1280px screen, and the elimination run dead-ended with one child left whom the app refused to pick. She would use it once and go back to popsicle sticks, which is exactly the competitor the research names as the real one.

frictions.what: Nowhere to save a class list. storage() returns 0 bytes — the app writes nothing to localStorage. State lives only in the URL hash (index.html loads it once at app.js:148). To reuse tomorrow's roster she must bookmark a link and find it again.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research lists 'multiple named wheels that persist' as table stakes and quotes a reviewer who quit after their wheels disappeared. Maren has five sections; she gets zero. Typing 28 names in front of a class is the single documented moment a teacher closes the tab.

frictions.what: On the panel the wheel is capped at 380px wide (index.html:1253, .wheelwrap{max-width:380px}) on a 1280px screen, and with 28 names the labels render at a measured 6.3 CSS px. Measured, not estimated: canvas font is min(34, max(14, 320/n)) at app.js:65, drawn on a 760px backing canvas displayed at 380px, so every label is halved.
frictions.whyItMatters: Nobody past the second row can read who is on the wheel, so the wheel stops being the fairness theatre it is for. The research's whole design consequence section is 'contrast tuned for projector washout' and 'legibility at scale'.

frictions.what: The winner reveal is 24px at every viewport — measured 24px at 320px, 414px and 1280px (index.html:1260, #winner{font-size:1.5rem}). At Largest text it reaches 36px and stops.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research quotes a reviewer verbatim: 'Why doesn't the name pop up big after spinning... that's what I need, so people see the name pop up.' The stated target is 8-12vw, which is 102-154px at 1280. The app delivers 24px. The winner reveal is the product and it is the smallest thing on the page.

frictions.what: Elimination dead-ends. With 'Remove the winner' on and two names left, one spin removes one — and the next spin refuses with the toast 'Add at least two names' (app.js:78). Verified: 3 names went 3 -> 2 -> 1 and the last child was never picked.
frictions.whyItMatters: The last student is the one who has been waiting the whole time. The app tells the teacher off instead of announcing them, in front of the class. The research calls elimination 'the primary classroom mode', not an edge case.

frictions.what: 'Restore removed names' is armed by a variable that any keystroke wipes: the textarea input handler sets removed = [] (app.js:121). Verified — spin with removal on, then type one extra name, then press Restore, and it says 'Nobody has been removed yet'.
frictions.whyItMatters: Adding the late arrival is the most ordinary classroom edit there is, and it silently destroys the undo for the whole period. There is no warning.

frictions.what: No count anywhere. Verified: no '/\d+ names/' text exists in the DOM at any list size. The research asks for a live count and an 'X of 28 left' counter.
frictions.whyItMatters: Mid-elimination she cannot tell how many are left without counting textarea lines, and she cannot tell that the list she pasted was silently cut (see Tom).

frictions.what: Restoring reorders. After removals, Restore does names.concat(removed) (app.js:133), so an alphabetical roster comes back as B|A|C — verified.
frictions.whyItMatters: A register is alphabetical for a reason; she now cannot scan it to see who is missing.

delights: Zero setup and zero chrome: the SPIN button is on screen at load, full width, 52px tall, with nothing to dismiss first. No cookie banner, no rating nag, no ad — exactly the promise the research says the whole category violates.
The removal toggle is on the main screen with plain-language copy ('great for classrooms & raffles'), not buried in settings.
The wheel and the announced winner genuinely agree. Sampled the canvas pixel directly under the pointer on four spins and it matched the winning slice's colour 4/4 — the pick is honest.

personas.name: Devon Reyes
personas.who: 29, variety streamer, ~600 concurrent. High technical confidence, runs OBS with browser sources, chat is primed to shout 'rigged'. Drawn from the research's second named user.
personas.context: Seated, dark room, second monitor, wheel as a 900x900 OBS browser source. Mid-stream, must not alt-tab away from the game. Wants it silent.
personas.task: Run a 40-entry sub-goal wheel three times during a stream and be able to prove to chat that it was fair.
personas.verdict: Usable as a novelty, not as a stream tool. The fixed 4.25-second spin, the absence of any hotkey, the 380px cap and the absence of a result log mean he'd keep the wheel he already has. He specifically noticed there is no receipt to point chat at.

frictions.what: Spin duration is hardcoded at dur = 4200 (app.js:85) with no UI to change it — measured 4252ms wall time, and no /speed|duration|fast/ text exists anywhere in the page.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research quotes exactly this: 'it wouldn't be so bad if the spin wasn't so long... it could at least go faster.' Three spins is thirteen seconds of dead air on a live stream.

frictions.what: No spin history and no fairness receipt. #winner is overwritten on the next spin (app.js:81) and nothing is retained. Nothing to screenshot for chat.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research documents live 'is this rigged' suspicion (r/AskPC, r/UnethicalLifeProTips) and notes competitors already market 'CSPRNG' and 'provably random'. A visible timestamped log is the differentiator and it is absent.

frictions.what: Randomness is Math.random (app.js:82-83), not crypto.getRandomValues — confirmed by reading the shipped app.js in-page. Distribution itself is fine: 20,000 simulated spins across 10 slices gave 1903-2093 per slice, max deviation 4.9% (~2.3 sigma), no structural bias.
frictions.whyItMatters: Mechanically honest, rhetorically weak. He cannot answer chat with anything better than 'trust me', when the thing that would answer it is a two-line change.

frictions.what: No keyboard trigger he can use twice. Pressing Space on SPIN disables the button (app.js:80), which throws focus to <body> — verified, activeElement is BODY both during and after the spin. A second Space does nothing.
frictions.whyItMatters: A hotkey-driven spin is the entire OBS use case. Instead every spin requires re-Tabbing three times from the top of the document.

frictions.what: The hub of the wheel is a hardcoded white disc, ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff' (app.js:72-73) — sampled rgb(255,255,255) at the centre in dark mode — and the segment palette is six hardcoded hex values (helpers.js:43) with no transparent-background or theme option.
frictions.whyItMatters: A blazing white dot in a dark overlay, and no way to key it out or match his scene palette. The research names the transparent OBS background as a differentiator.

frictions.what: The QR dialog heading is invisible in dark mode: dialog background computed rgb(18,18,18), h3 colour rgb(17,17,17) (index.html:1314, inline style="color:#111") — roughly 1.0:1.
frictions.whyItMatters: The dialog looks broken. It is one hardcoded hex that escaped the token system.

delights: It really is one file that runs with no account, no login and no platform tie — the exact thing the research says third-party stream wheels lead their marketing with.
Service worker installs cleanly (cache wheel-v14, 11 assets) and a reload with the network cut still boots the app. Verified offline. That is the 'never fails mid-stream' promise, delivered.

personas.name: Priya Raman
personas.who: 55, PTA fundraising volunteer. Low vision — runs her phone at maximum system text and needs about 200% to read comfortably. Moderate tech confidence. She is the persona the comfort panel exists for.
personas.context: Standing at a raffle table in a school hall, phone in one hand, clipboard in the other, people waiting. Bright hall lighting, one-handed.
personas.task: Draw six raffle winners from a list of 120 ticket-holder names she has in an email, and read each winner out loud.
personas.verdict: The comfort panel did its job on the page and could do nothing about the product. She turned text to Largest and the page obeyed — body 16px -> 24px, winner 24px -> 36px, and the layout held with zero horizontal overflow. But the wheel itself is a canvas the panel cannot touch, so the names she needs to read stayed at 11.9 CSS px. She ended up reading winners off the textarea, not the wheel.

frictions.what: The comfort panel cannot enlarge the one thing that matters. After setting Largest, measured: body 24px, #winner 36px, SPIN button still 52px tall, canvas still 340px wide, and the on-wheel label size unchanged at 11.9px for a 12-name wheel. The canvas font is computed in app.js:65 from name count only — it never reads the text preference or the root font size.
frictions.whyItMatters: A low-vision user turns text up and the app's central object visibly ignores her. This is the comfort panel failing at its stated purpose in the one app where the content is drawn rather than typeset.

frictions.what: Her 120-name list was silently cut to 100. parseNames slices at 100 (helpers.js:5) and truncates each name to 40 characters (helpers.js:6). Verified: 500 pasted names became exactly 100 with no message, no count, no highlight.
frictions.whyItMatters: Twenty ticket-holders who paid were never in the draw and nobody could have known. The research's loudest feature complaint is entry caps ('you can't even put ten options without paying') — this app has an invisible cap of its own.

frictions.what: The 40-character truncation makes the textarea and the wheel disagree. Verified: 'Bartholomew Fitzgerald-Wellingtonshire III' stays whole in the textarea but is stored and shared as 'Bartholomew Fitzgerald-Wellingtonshire I'.
frictions.whyItMatters: The list she is reading from and the list being drawn are different lists, and the shared link carries the mangled version.

frictions.what: The 'Remove the winner' checkbox is a 13x20px hit target (index.html:1298) — under the 44px floor on every viewport tested, including at Largest text where it only reaches 13x30.
frictions.whyItMatters: One-handed, standing, with a clipboard, she has to hit the label text instead. The label does work as a target, which saves it from being major.

delights: The comfort panel itself is genuinely well built and she noticed. It opens from the header, focus lands on the Close button, there is a live type sample so she can see the effect without closing, Done returns focus to the trigger button, and axe reported zero violations with the panel open.
Everything held at 320px with Largest text and Roomy spacing simultaneously — overflow() returned 0 in all seven viewport/preference combinations tested. No sideways scroll anywhere.
White-on-fill labels are honestly contrasty: measured 5.02:1 to 7.58:1 against all six segment colours, all passing WCAG AA.

personas.name: Tom Whitlock
personas.who: 34, supply/substitute teacher, low-to-moderate tech confidence, first day in an unfamiliar school. Uses the keyboard because the borrowed Chromebook's trackpad is unreliable.
personas.context: Borrowed Chromebook plugged into a projector, filtered school Wi-Fi, first period, 31 kids he does not know. Two hands on the keyboard.
personas.task: Pick a random order for 31 children to present, using only the keyboard.
personas.verdict: He completed one spin and then got stuck in a loop. He could not work out why pressing Space again did nothing, and did not realise he had to Tab three times from the top of the page after every single spin. He gave up after four names and read down the register instead.

frictions.what: Focus is destroyed by the main action. $('spinBtn').disabled = true (app.js:80) while the button holds focus, so the browser moves focus to <body>. Verified: activeElement is BODY during the spin and still BODY 4.5 seconds later, when the button has been re-enabled. Pressing Space then does nothing.
frictions.whyItMatters: The core job cannot be repeated by keyboard without re-traversing the whole document each time. For a switch or keyboard user this makes the app effectively single-use per page load. Nothing in axe catches it — axe returned zero violations on load, after interaction, and with the panel open.

frictions.what: No skip link. The .skip component is styled at index.html:840 and hidden in the print block at 1196, and <main id="main"> exists at index.html:1280, but no skip element is ever rendered. First Tab lands on the comfort-settings button.
frictions.whyItMatters: Small page, so the cost is small — but the component is already paid for and simply not used, and this app is the one where re-Tabbing happens on every spin.

frictions.what: His 31 names pasted from two class lists came to 120 lines with some blanks and got cut to 100 with no notice (helpers.js:5). Duplicates were kept silently too — 'Sam' four times stays four slices and the DOM contains no 'duplicate' notice.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research asks specifically for a dedupe with an undoable notice and a live count. A substitute has no way to know the wheel does not match the register.

frictions.what: Pasting a shared wheel link into the address bar of an already-open tab does nothing. app.js:148 reads location.hash once at init and there is no hashchange listener. Verified: changing the hash to a Kim/Lee/Max wheel left the textarea showing Ana|Ben.
frictions.whyItMatters: The app's entire persistence story is 'the wheel lives in the link', and the most obvious way to open a link — pasting it into the tab you already have open — silently fails. After a Back press the URL and the visible wheel disagree outright.

delights: It worked on the filtered network, and it kept working with the network off entirely. Verified offline reload boots the full UI.
Nothing he typed was lost: the list survives reload, including a half-typed name, and even a reload mid-spin comes back with the roster intact (only the winner line clears, which is correct).

personas.name: Bea Lindqvist
personas.who: 68, grandmother, essential tremor in her right hand and a history of vestibular migraine — spinning motion on screen can trigger an episode. Low tech confidence. She has 'reduce motion' switched on at the OS level because she has been told to.
personas.context: iPad on the kitchen table at 320px-equivalent width in Split View, warm evening light, one finger, not in a hurry but easily knocked off target.
personas.task: Spin a five-item chore wheel with her grandchildren after dinner.
personas.verdict: It worked and it made her feel unwell. She had 'reduce motion' on at the OS level and Reduced set in the app's own Motion preference, and the wheel still performed a full 4.27-second rotation. She looked away from the screen for the second spin, which rather defeats the point of watching a wheel with your grandchildren.

frictions.what: prefers-reduced-motion and the app's own Motion=Reduced preference are both ignored by the spin. Verified: with prefs {motion:'less'} (data-motion="less" on <html>) AND page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}), the spin still ran 4273ms of continuous rotation. app.js:82-91 goes straight to requestAnimationFrame with no media query or attribute check.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is a health issue, not a taste issue, and the research names it as a differentiator: 'Nobody in this category treats a spinning disc as the accessibility problem it is.' The app ships the comfort panel that promises to control motion and then does not honour it in the one component that moves.

frictions.what: No reduced-motion alternative reveal exists at all — there is no non-rotating path to a winner in the code.
frictions.whyItMatters: Turning motion off cannot mean losing the feature. The research suggests a shuffle-and-settle; there is nothing.

frictions.what: Her tremor made the 13x20px removal checkbox (index.html:1298) a miss every time, and there is no undo for accidentally toggling it — toggling it mid-spin actually changed the outcome. Verified: checking 'Remove the winner' 800ms into a running spin caused that spin's winner to be deleted from the list.
frictions.whyItMatters: A stray tap during the four seconds when the user is watching the wheel silently deletes a name. The setting should be read when the spin starts, not when it ends.

frictions.what: The empty state is a 12.5 CSS px line of canvas text reading 'Add names below' (app.js:41-42 draws it at 28px on the 760px backing canvas).
frictions.whyItMatters: It is the first thing a new user sees and it is the smallest text on the page. She did not see it and asked what she was supposed to do.

delights: The warm tint and dark theme both looked right to her, and the page background gradient is properly theme-aware.
Nothing interrupted her. No modal, no prompt, no ad, ever — the research's 'absolute no-interruption rule' is actually kept.

personas.name: Aisha Bello
personas.who: 16, sixth-former running a charity raffle. High phone confidence, expects to share things the way she shares everything — a link in a group chat or a QR on a poster.
personas.context: iPhone at 414px, one thumb, in a noisy common room between lessons. Two minutes before the bell.
personas.task: Build a 100-name raffle wheel and get it onto a poster as a QR code plus into the year-group chat as a link.
personas.verdict: Failed at the share step, which is the step this app is built around. The QR simply refused for her real list, with an error toast and no explanation of what to do instead.

frictions.what: 'Show QR' fails for real rosters. With 100 realistic-length names the URL reaches 5,788 characters, qrcode() throws, and the app shows the toast 'Could not draw the QR' and never opens the dialog (app.js:162-177). Verified — the QR canvas was left entirely blank.
frictions.whyItMatters: The toast names the symptom and not the cause or the cure. She has no idea that shortening the list would fix it, so she concludes the app is broken. Measured URL growth: 4 names = 119 chars, 28 = 528, 60 = 1,083, 100 = 1,777 with short names, 5,788 with 40-char names.

frictions.what: Nothing warns that a link is getting too long to share before she hits the wall — no length indicator, no 'too long for a QR' hint next to the button.
frictions.whyItMatters: The failure arrives at the last possible moment, in front of an audience, which the research identifies as this category's characteristic failure mode.

frictions.what: 'Copy link to this wheel' quietly produces a 5.7KB URL. It copies fine, but a URL that long is mangled by several chat clients and cannot go on a poster at all.
frictions.whyItMatters: The promise in the hint text at index.html:1305 — 'bookmark your class list, share the chore wheel' — is only true up to a size the app never states.

delights: For a small wheel the share flow is genuinely delightful: four names, an 88-character URL, an instant QR, and the dialog closes on Escape with focus returning correctly to the Show QR button.
She liked that the link is the save file. No account, nothing to sign up for — the exact thing the research says mobile users praise.

worksWell: It opens spin-ready with no interruption of any kind — no ad, no rating nag, no cookie banner, no onboarding. Every persona noticed and none of them had anything to dismiss.
The privacy and offline story is real, not marketing: storage() shows 0 bytes written, the service worker caches 11 assets as wheel-v14, and a reload with the network cut boots the full working app.

Layout is genuinely bulletproof. overflow() returned 0 at 320px, 414px, 1280px, at Largest text, at Roomy spacing, at both simultaneously, in dark scheme and at warmth 3 with high contrast. Not one offender in any combination.
Accessibility of the typeset UI is clean: axe found zero WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA violations on load, after a full spin, and with the comfort dialog open.

The pick is honest and provably so. Sampling the canvas pixel under the pointer matched the winning slice's colour on 4/4 spins, and 20,000 simulated spins over 10 slices deviated at most 4.9% (~2.3 sigma) from even.

Input handling is safe and fast. '<script>alert(1)</script>' round-trips as literal text via textContent, whitespace-only lines are dropped, RTL and emoji survive, and pasting 500 names costs 8.2ms in-page with a 2.59ms redraw at 100 names.

Nothing is lost on reload — the URL hash restores the roster, a half-typed name and the removal toggle — and corrupt input is handled without a single console error across seven malformed-hash cases including 5,000 names and non-base64 garbage.
The comfort panel is exemplary as a component: header-mounted, focus to Close on open, live type sample, focus returned to the trigger on Done, and axe-clean.
hurts: The comfort panel cannot reach the wheel. Text size, contrast and motion preferences all stop at the edge of the canvas — labels stay 6-15 CSS px, the disc stays 380px, and a 4.27-second rotation runs even with Reduced motion set in the panel AND prefers-reduced-motion at the OS level.
The winner reveal — which the research calls the product — is 24px at every viewport, 36px at maximum text. On a 1280px projector that is a fifth of the size the category needs.
There is a hard, silent 100-name cap and a silent 40-character-per-name truncation (helpers.js:5-6). No count, no notice, and the textarea and the wheel end up showing different names.
Keyboard users cannot spin twice. Disabling the focused SPIN button throws focus to <body>, and the second Space press does nothing.
Elimination mode dead-ends: the last remaining person can never be picked, and the app scolds with 'Add at least two names' instead of announcing them.
'Restore removed names' is silently disarmed by any keystroke in the textarea, and restoring reorders the list.
The whole persistence story rests on one URL hash: no named wheels, no export, no import, and pasting a shared link into an already-open tab does nothing because there is no hashchange listener.
Sharing breaks at real scale: 100 names produces a 5.7KB URL and the QR fails with 'Could not draw the QR' and no explanation.
'🎉 undefined' can reach the winner line — clear the textarea while the wheel is spinning and that is what the class sees.

The six segment colours are all the same lightness. Adjacent-pair contrast measures 1.04:1 to 1.47:1, so the wheel reads as one mid-tone blur on a washed-out projector and to a red-green colourblind viewer.
Print produces a full-colour wheel, a SPIN button and a textarea clipped to 104px of the 718px it needs — 4 of 28 names make it onto the paper.
The QR dialog heading is invisible in dark mode: rgb(17,17,17) on rgb(18,18,18), from one inline hex at index.html:1314.
mostWantedNext: A presentation mode: chrome gone, wheel filling the screen, winner at 8-12vw, held until dismissed.
Saved, named wheels with rename/duplicate/delete, plus export and import to a file — the backup story that local-only storage obliges.
Paste-a-spreadsheet import that splits on commas, semicolons and tabs as well as newlines, with a live count and an undoable dedupe notice.
Real elimination: picked names greyed on the wheel rather than deleted, an 'X of 28 left' counter, a final spin that names the last person, and a one-tap 'Reset for next period'.
An honest reduced-motion path — a shuffle-and-settle reveal with no rotation — plus a spin-speed control.
A session log of results with timestamps, copyable as text: the fairness receipt for chat and for the staffroom.
A spacebar hotkey and a transparent-background option for OBS.
Printable output: a numbered roster and cut-up slips, for the day the projector bulb dies.
Group/team split ('turn these 28 into 7 groups of 4') — the one feature the research says teachers leave a wheel app to go and find.
The IT-approval sentence at the top of the page, copyable for a district software-request form.

scenarios.name: A lot of data — 500 names
scenarios.method: withApp('wheel-picker'): page.fill('#names', 500 lines of 'Student N Lastname'), then decode the URL hash to count what actually reached the wheel; separately timed the in-page cost by setting textarea.value and dispatching 'input' inside page.evaluate, and averaged 60 successive redraws at 100 names.
scenarios.result: Exactly 100 of 500 names reached the wheel (helpers.js:5 .slice(0,100)); the other 400 vanished with no message. No count is displayed anywhere — a /\d+\s+names?/ regex over document.innerText finds nothing. Performance is excellent: 8.2ms for parse+hash+draw of 500 names, 2.59ms average redraw at 100 names, overflow() still 0.
scenarios.defect: Silent 100-entry cap with no notice and no visible count. Performance is not the problem; honesty is.

scenarios.name: Hostile text
scenarios.method: Filled #names with a 2000-char line, a 500-char single word, '', '', emoji with ZWJ sequences, Arabic RTL, whitespace-only lines, tabs, accented duplicates and a 41-char name. Then spun with 'bold' as a name and inspected #winner.innerHTML.
scenarios.result: No XSS: #winner.innerHTML came back '🎉 <b>bold</b>' with 0 child elements — textContent is used throughout (app.js:98). Whitespace-only and tab-only lines were correctly dropped. Emoji, ZWJ sequences and RTL survived intact. The 2000-char and 500-char entries were both silently cut to 40 chars (helpers.js:6). overflow() stayed 0. Zero console errors.
scenarios.defect: Only the silent 40-char truncation, which desynchronises the textarea from the wheel and from the shared link. Escaping, whitespace, emoji and RTL all handled correctly.

scenarios.name: Numeric edges as entries
scenarios.method: The app takes no numeric input field, so the numeric surface is entry text and the URL hash. Entered '0', '-1', '1e9', '0.0001', 'abc', 'NaN', 'Infinity', '-0' as names and spun; then scanned document.innerText for NaN/Infinity.
scenarios.result: All eight were treated as opaque strings and one was announced as '🎉 Infinity' — the literal text the user typed, correctly. No computed NaN or Infinity reached the UI from any code path. Zero console errors.

scenarios.name: Duplicate and identical entries
scenarios.method: Filled #names with 'Sam' four times, then with 'Zoë'/'Zoë'/'ZOË'; checked for any dedupe notice in the DOM and inspected the parsed list.
scenarios.result: All duplicates kept as separate slices, which is defensible (a raffle may want weighted repeats), but there is no dedupe notice, no count and no indication anywhere — document.innerText contains no 'duplicate'. The research asks specifically for 'removed 2 duplicates' with an undo.
scenarios.defect: No dedupe affordance and no count, so an accidental double-paste is invisible.

scenarios.name: Rapid interaction — SPIN clicked 30x
scenarios.method: Five names loaded, then 30 page.click('#spinBtn', {force:true}) in a tight loop, checking button state mid-flight and after settle.
scenarios.result: 30 clicks dispatched in 261ms. The spinning guard (app.js:77) held perfectly: the button was disabled throughout, exactly one spin ran, and one winner ('🎉 A') was announced after settle with the button re-enabled. No double-submit, no stacked animations, no console errors.

scenarios.name: Editing the list while the wheel is spinning
scenarios.method: Started a spin, then 900-1000ms in: (a) cleared #names entirely, (b) shrank a 20-name list to 2, (c) checked #removeMode mid-spin. Read #winner after settle each time.
scenarios.result: (a) Winner announced as '🎉 undefined' — sliceAtPointer returns -1 for count 0 (helpers.js:13) and app.js:96-98 indexes names[-1] without a guard. (b) Shrinking 20 to 2 resolved to a valid entry, 'X'. (c) Toggling removal mid-spin retroactively applied it — 'Cleo' was announced and deleted from the list even though the toggle was off when the spin began.
scenarios.defect: '🎉 undefined' shown to the room; and removeMode is read at settle time (app.js:99) rather than at spin start, so a stray tap during the 4.2s animation deletes a name.

scenarios.name: Elimination mode run to exhaustion
scenarios.method: Three names, #removeMode checked, spun repeatedly to the end; then two names, spun once, spun again; then pressed #resetBtn; then repeated with a keystroke in the textarea between the spin and the reset.
scenarios.result: 3 -> 2 -> 1 and then stuck: with one name left, SPIN refuses with the toast 'Add at least two names' (app.js:78), so the last person is never picked and never announced. Restore works when untouched but reorders (A,B,C came back as B|A|C, app.js:133). After any keystroke in the textarea, Restore reports 'Nobody has been removed yet' because the input handler resets removed=[] (app.js:121).
scenarios.defect: Elimination dead-ends one short, and the restore buffer is destroyed by ordinary editing with no warning.

scenarios.name: 320px, and 414px at text=xxl and at density=roomy
scenarios.method: Seven separate withApp runs with a 28-name roster loaded: 320px; 414px prefs{text:'xxl'}; 414px prefs{density:'roomy'}; 320px with both; dark scheme; prefs{warmth:'3',contrast:'more'}; 1280px. overflow() and offenders() in each.
scenarios.result: overflow() = 0 in all seven; offenders() never invoked because nothing overflowed. Metrics — 320px: wheel 246px, SPIN 246x52, winner 24px. 414/xxl: body 16->24px, winner 24->36px, wheel unchanged at 340px, SPIN still 52px tall. 414/roomy: wheel 322px, winner 24px. 320+xxl+roomy: wheel 228px, clean. 1280px: wheel capped at 380px, winner still 24px. smallTargets is the same short list everywhere: #swsPrefsBtn 36x36, #tipLink 36 tall, #removeMode 13x20, and two 20px-tall footer links.
scenarios.defect: No layout defect at all. But the canvas ignores every comfort preference, and the wheel never exceeds 380px however wide the screen (index.html:1253), so a projector gets a phone-sized wheel and 24px winner text.

scenarios.name: Dark scheme and warmth:'3'
scenarios.method: withApp with scheme:'dark' and separately prefs{warmth:'3',contrast:'more'}; sampled canvas pixels and computed styles; opened the QR dialog in dark.
scenarios.result: Page theming is correct — body rgb(27,17,21), --chip #30242a, empty-disc pixel sampled rgba(48,36,42,255) meaning the placeholder correctly picks up the dark token. Warmth 3 + high contrast: overflow 0, no visual break. Two hardcoded values escape the system: the wheel hub is ctx.fillStyle='#ffffff' (app.js:72-73), sampled rgb(255,255,255) — a bright white disc in a dark room; and the QR dialog heading computes to rgb(17,17,17) on a rgb(18,18,18) dialog background (index.html:1314, inline color:#111), roughly 1.0:1 and unreadable.
scenarios.defect: Invisible QR dialog heading in dark mode; hardcoded white wheel hub.

scenarios.name: Segment colour contrast
scenarios.method: Computed WCAG relative luminance and contrast ratios for the six WHEEL_COLORS (helpers.js:43) against the white label fill, and for each adjacent pair as drawn by sliceColor.
scenarios.result: Label legibility passes comfortably: #2563eb 5.17:1, #0f766e 5.47:1, #7c3aed 5.70:1, #b45309 5.02:1, #be185d 6.04:1, #475569 7.58:1 — all above 4.5:1. But adjacent wedges are near-identical in lightness: 1.06, 1.04, 1.13, 1.20, 1.26 and 1.47:1. The only separation is a 2px rgba(255,255,255,.35) stroke.
scenarios.defect: Wedge-to-wedge separation rests on hue alone, which fails for red-green colourblind viewers and washes out on a projector — exactly what the research's colorRecommendation warns against.

scenarios.name: Legibility at scale
scenarios.method: Loaded 6, 24, 40 and 100 names and computed each label's rendered CSS size from app.js:65's formula times the canvas display scale (760px backing canvas shown at 340px on a 414px phone).
scenarios.result: 6 names: 60° wedges, 34px canvas font = 15.2 CSS px. 24 names: 15° wedges, 14px = 6.3 CSS px. 40 names: 9° wedges, labels cut to 10 chars, 6.3 CSS px. 100 names: 3.6° wedges, 10 chars, 6.3 CSS px. The font formula bottoms out at 14px canvas (6.3 CSS px) from 23 names upward and never recovers.
scenarios.defect: Above ~20 names the wheel is decorative — the labels cannot be read on a phone, let alone from the back of a classroom. 'Unlimited entries' rendered as unreadable slivers is the exact failure the research names.

scenarios.name: Reload mid-task and mid-spin
scenarios.method: Typed names, started a spin, reloaded 1.2s into it; separately reloaded with a half-typed name ('Cle', no trailing newline); separately toggled #removeMode and reloaded.
scenarios.result: Everything the user typed survived: roster intact after a mid-spin reload, the half-typed 'Cle' preserved, #removeMode still checked. #winner correctly cleared (an interrupted spin should not claim a result). localStorage stayed at 0 bytes — all state is the URL hash.

scenarios.name: localStorage size and corruption
scenarios.method: Called storage() after heavy use; set localStorage['sws.prefs'] = '{{{not json' and reloaded; the app itself owns no localStorage key, so also corrupted its real persistence surface — seven malformed URL hashes on genuine fresh loads (about:blank between each, since a hash-only change is a same-document navigation and does not re-init).
scenarios.result: storage() = 0 bytes after every scenario — this app writes nothing to localStorage, so there is no key to corrupt and no growth to worry about. Corrupt sws.prefs: app loaded normally, data-text attribute absent, no error. Hash cases all handled cleanly with zero console errors: non-base64 garbage -> empty, valid base64 that is not JSON -> empty, {"n":"Ana"} (not an array) -> empty, mixed types [1,2,{},null,"Real"] -> just 'Real' kept, deep nesting -> fine, 5,000 names -> 100 kept in 247ms, bare '#' -> empty.

scenarios.name: Hash navigation and the Back button
scenarios.method: With the app open and a wheel loaded, set location.hash to a different encoded wheel (what happens when a user pastes a shared link into the tab they already have open); then made edits and pressed Back.
scenarios.result: Hash swap changed the URL and did nothing to the app — the textarea still read 'Ana|Ben'. app.js:148 reads the hash once in init() and there is no hashchange listener. After Back, the URL showed the older encoded state while the textarea showed the newer one: the address bar and the visible wheel disagreed. syncHash uses history.replaceState (app.js:113) so Back does not act as undo either.
scenarios.defect: The app's only persistence mechanism cannot be re-entered while the app is open, and Back silently desynchronises the URL from the wheel — a bookmark taken at that moment saves the wrong list.

scenarios.name: Share link and QR at real roster sizes
scenarios.method: Measured location.href.length at 4/12/28/60/100 names, then clicked #qrBtn with 100 forty-character names and again with 4 names; counted dark pixels in #qrCanvas and checked dialog state, Escape handling and focus return.
scenarios.result: URL length: 4 names 119 chars, 12 = 251, 28 = 528, 60 = 1,083, 100 short names = 1,777, 100 long names = 5,788. At 5,788 chars qrcode() threw, the catch at app.js:174 fired, the toast said 'Could not draw the QR', the dialog never opened and the canvas was left completely blank (0 drawn pixels). With 4 names the QR drew correctly (30,096 dark pixels), the dialog opened, Escape closed it, and focus returned properly to #qrBtn.
scenarios.defect: QR generation fails silently-ish for realistic class rosters with a message that explains nothing and offers no fallback; no warning that the link is approaching unusable length.

scenarios.name: Keyboard only, end to end
scenarios.method: Tabbed through the whole document recording activeElement; typed the roster with the keyboard; pressed Space on SPIN; checked focus during and after the spin; pressed Space again.
scenarios.result: Tab order is logical: #swsPrefsBtn, #tipLink, #spinBtn, #names, #removeMode, #shareBtn, #qrBtn, #resetBtn, then the two footer links. No skip link is rendered (the .skip component is styled at index.html:840 and <main id="main"> exists at 1280, but no element uses it). The core job is reachable — but only once. Disabling the focused button at app.js:80 sends focus to <body>, where it remains after the spin completes, and a second Space does nothing. Every subsequent spin needs three Tabs from the top.
scenarios.defect: Focus is destroyed by the primary action, making repeated spinning impossible by keyboard without re-traversal. Plus the missing skip link.

scenarios.name: Reduced motion
scenarios.method: withApp with prefs{motion:'less'} (confirmed data-motion="less" on <html>) AND page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}), then timed a spin from click to the button re-enabling.
scenarios.result: 4,273ms of continuous rotation — statistically identical to the 4,252ms measured with motion at default. app.js:82-91 consults neither the media query nor the data-motion attribute, and there is no alternative reveal path in the code. There is also no UI to shorten the spin: no /speed|duration|fast/ text exists anywhere in the page.
scenarios.defect: Both the OS-level preference and the app's own comfort setting are ignored by the only moving element in the app.

scenarios.name: axe after interaction, not just on load
scenarios.method: axe() with wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa/22aa on first load, after typing a roster and completing a full spin with a winner displayed, and again with the comfort dialog open.
scenarios.result: Zero violations in all three states. The comfort dialog's visually-hidden 1x1 radio inputs are correctly labelled and did not trip anything.

scenarios.name: Print
scenarios.method: page.emulateMedia({media:'print'}) with a 28-name roster; inspected computed display of every region and compared the textarea's rendered height to its scrollHeight.
scenarios.result: header.app and footer.colophon are correctly hidden, as are #swsPrefsBtn and the prefs dialog (index.html:1197). But the SPIN button still prints as inline-flex, the three action buttons print, the .hint paragraph prints, the full-colour 380px wheel prints, and #names prints at 104px against a scrollHeight of 718px — roughly 4 of 28 names reach the paper, the rest clipped away with no scrollbar to hint at it.
scenarios.defect: Printing produces a page of dead buttons, a colour disc and a truncated list. There is no printable roster or slip output, which the research names as a differentiator ('degrade gracefully to paper').

scenarios.name: Fairness — distribution and pointer truth
scenarios.method: Ran 20,000 iterations of app.js's exact target formula through the shipped sliceAtPointer for a 10-slice wheel; then spun the real UI four times and sampled the canvas pixel directly beneath the pointer, comparing it to sliceColor(index of announced winner).
scenarios.result: Distribution [2011, 2012, 1981, 2003, 2016, 2050, 2093, 2004, 1927, 1903] — max deviation 4.9% (~2.3 sigma at n=2000), no structural bias. Pointer truth: 4/4 spins, the pixel under the pointer exactly matched the announced winner's slice colour. Randomness source is Math.random (app.js:82-83), not crypto.getRandomValues, confirmed by reading the served app.js.
scenarios.defect: Mechanically sound — no rigging, no off-by-one. What is missing is the evidence: no CSPRNG claim to make, and no session log for a streamer to point chat at or a teacher to show a parent.

scenarios.name: Offline / service worker
scenarios.method: Waited on navigator.serviceWorker.ready, enumerated the cache contents, then set the browser context offline and reloaded the app.
scenarios.result: Registered at the app scope with an active worker; cache 'wheel-v14' holds all 11 declared assets including sws-ui.js, sws-prefs.js and the woff2. With the network off, a full reload rendered the working UI. Note: sws-ui.js was regenerated into the app mid-review (15:10) — had it still been missing, cache.addAll would have rejected and offline support would have been dead, which is worth a guard.

scenarios.name: Comfort panel, driven for real
scenarios.method: Opened #swsPrefsBtn from the header, enumerated the controls, selected 'Largest', ran axe with the dialog open, closed via Done, then measured body/#winner/SPIN/canvas and recomputed the on-wheel label size.
scenarios.result: The panel works: dialog.open true, focus lands on the Close button, all seven groups present (theme/text/density/reading/warmth/contrast/motion), axe clean, Done returns focus to #swsPrefsBtn, data-text='xxl' persisted. Effects: body 16 -> 24px, #winner 24 -> 36px. Non-effects: canvas stays 340px, SPIN stays 52px tall, and the on-wheel labels are computed purely from name count (app.js:65) so they do not change at all.
scenarios.defect: The panel is well built and reaches everything except the app's central object. For a low-vision user the names on the wheel are the content, and they are the one thing no preference can enlarge.

fixes.title: Honour reduced motion in the spin, and add a spin-speed control
fixes.rationale: Bea has vestibular migraine, had prefers-reduced-motion set at the OS level AND Motion=Reduced in the app's own comfort panel, and still got a measured 4,273ms of continuous rotation — indistinguishable from the 4,252ms default. Shipping a comfort panel with a Motion group and then ignoring it in the only moving element is worse than not offering it. Devon separately needs the spin shorter; the research quotes 'it wouldn't be so bad if the spin wasn't so long'. Fix both with one control: read matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and document.documentElement.dataset.motion, and when either says reduce, replace the rotation with a shuffle-and-settle reveal (rapid label cycling for ~600ms, then land) rather than removing the feature.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:82-91 (spin's rAF loop and const dur = 4200)

fixes.title: Stop destroying keyboard focus on every spin
fixes.rationale: Verified: pressing Space on SPIN sets spinBtn.disabled = true while it holds focus, so the browser moves activeElement to <body> — and it is still <body> 4.5s later once the button is re-enabled. A second Space does nothing, so Tom had to Tab three times from the top of the document for every single spin and gave up after four names. Devon's whole OBS use case is a hotkey. axe cannot see this (it reported zero violations in all three states), so only a driven keyboard test catches it. Fix: keep the button enabled and guard on the existing `spinning` flag (it already returns early at app.js:77), setting aria-disabled and aria-busy instead of the disabled property; or move focus deliberately to #winner when the result lands. Add a document-level Space/Enter hotkey while nothing is focused in the textarea.

fixes.title: Make the winner reveal projector-sized, and let the wheel grow past 380px
fixes.rationale: Measured 24px winner text at 320px, 414px AND 1280px — the same 1.5rem everywhere (36px at Largest text), while .wheelwrap caps the disc at 380px no matter how wide the screen. Maren is 8-12 feet from a wall panel with 28 children watching; the research quotes a reviewer directly on this — 'Why doesn't the name pop up big after spinning... that's what I need, so people see the name pop up' — and sets the target at 8-12vw, which is 102-154px at 1280. Fix: clamp() the winner to something like clamp(2rem, 9vw, 9rem) as a full-bleed held card, and let .wheelwrap scale with min(90vw, 70vh) above a tablet breakpoint. This is the cheapest change with the largest effect on whether the app is usable for its primary persona.

fixes.title: Tell the user about the 100-name cap and the 40-character truncation — or lift them
fixes.rationale: Verified: 500 pasted names silently became exactly 100, and 'Bartholomew Fitzgerald-Wellingtonshire III' is stored and shared as 'Bartholomew Fitzgerald-Wellingtonshire I' while the textarea still shows it whole. Priya's 120 raffle entrants became 100 and twenty paying ticket-holders were never in the draw; nobody could have known, because no count is rendered anywhere in the DOM at any list size. The research's loudest feature complaint in the whole category is entry caps ('you can't even put ten options without paying'), and it names 'unlimited, and say the word unlimited' as the answer. Fix: raise the cap to whatever stays legible after the label fix, show a live 'N names' count next to the heading, and when anything is dropped or shortened say so in a toast with an undo (sws-ui.js's SWS.undo is now loaded and unused).
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/helpers.js:5-6 (.slice(0, 100) and .map(s => s.slice(0, 40))); count belongs at index.html:1292

fixes.title: Fix elimination: announce the last person, grey instead of delete, add a counter and a reset
fixes.rationale: Verified: with removal on, three names go 3 -> 2 -> 1 and then SPIN refuses with 'Add at least two names' — the last child is never picked and never announced, in front of the class. Related and equally bad: any keystroke in the textarea sets removed = [] (app.js:121), so Maren adding a late arrival silently disarms 'Restore removed names' ('Nobody has been removed yet'), and Restore reorders an alphabetical register to B|A|C. The research calls elimination 'the primary classroom mode, not an advanced setting' and asks for picked names greyed on the wheel, an 'X of 28 left' counter and a one-tap reset. Fix: keep one array with a picked flag instead of two arrays, draw picked slices desaturated, exempt them from the pointer, allow the final spin to name the last entry, and reconcile the textarea on edit rather than clearing state.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:78 (the <2 guard), app.js:99-105 (removal), app.js:119-124 (input handler clearing `removed`), app.js:130-138 (resetBtn)

fixes.title: Make the wheel labels obey the comfort panel and stay readable past 20 names
fixes.rationale: Priya set text to Largest and measured: body 16 -> 24px, winner 24 -> 36px, on-wheel labels unchanged at 11.9 CSS px, canvas unchanged at 340px. The canvas font comes only from name count (app.js:65) and bottoms out at 14px canvas = 6.3 CSS px from about 23 names upward — at 24, 40 and 100 names it is 6.3px in every case, with labels cut to 10 characters. So the comfort panel cannot reach the app's central object, and 'unlimited entries' renders as unreadable slivers, which the research explicitly calls a broken promise. Fix: derive the label size from the canvas display width and the root font size (multiply by the data-text scale), drop labels entirely below a legible threshold and switch to a numbered-wedge plus legend layout above ~30 entries.

fixes.title: Guard the winner lookup so '🎉 undefined' can never be announced
fixes.rationale: Verified: clear the textarea while the wheel is spinning and the class sees '🎉 undefined'. sliceAtPointer returns -1 when count is 0 (helpers.js:13) and app.js indexes names[-1] with no check. A teacher fixing a typo during the four-second animation is an entirely ordinary act. Same code path, same fix window: removeMode is read at settle time (app.js:99), so checking the box mid-spin retroactively deletes that spin's winner — verified, 'Cleo' was announced and removed although the toggle was off when the spin began. Snapshot the entry list and the removal setting when the spin starts and resolve against that snapshot.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:96-99 (const idx = sliceAtPointer(...); const winner = names[idx])

fixes.title: Give the app a real save story: named wheels, autosave, export and import
fixes.rationale: storage() returns 0 bytes — the app persists nothing beyond the URL hash. Maren has five sections and gets one bookmark-able link; the research lists multiple named wheels with working rename/duplicate/delete as table stakes and quotes a reviewer who left after 'my wheels disappeared. I'm not going to redo my wheels again.' It also insists that with local-only storage, an explicit export-to-file plus matching import is the backup story, not a power feature. Fix: autosave the current wheel to localStorage on every edit, add a saved-wheels list with rename/duplicate/delete, keep the hash as the share format, and add Export all / Import from the same row as the share buttons.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:111-115 (syncHash is the entire persistence layer); UI belongs at index.html:1300-1304

fixes.title: Fail gracefully when the share link outgrows a QR, and warn before it does
fixes.rationale: Verified: 100 forty-character names produce a 5,788-character URL, qrcode() throws, and Aisha gets the toast 'Could not draw the QR' with a blank canvas, no dialog and no explanation — at the moment she is standing in front of her poster deadline. Measured growth: 4 names 119 chars, 28 = 528, 60 = 1,083, 100 short = 1,777. Small wheels work beautifully (88-char URL, instant QR, correct focus return on Escape), so the fix is the ceiling, not the feature. Fix: compute the payload length before generating, and above the practical QR limit either compress the payload or say the useful thing — 'This wheel is too big for a QR (100 names). Copy the link instead, or share a shorter list.'
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:162-177 (showQr and its catch), toast at app.js:174

fixes.title: Listen for hashchange, and stop Back from desynchronising the URL from the wheel
fixes.rationale: Verified: with the app open, changing location.hash to a different encoded wheel does nothing — the textarea still showed the old names, because app.js:148 reads the hash once in init() and nothing listens afterwards. Pasting a shared link into the tab you already have open is the most natural way to open a link, and this app's entire persistence pitch is 'the whole wheel lives inside the link' (index.html:1305). Worse, after Back the address bar showed one encoded state while the textarea showed another, so a bookmark taken at that moment saves the wrong list. Fix: add a hashchange listener that reloads state (guarding against the app's own replaceState writes), and consider pushState on meaningful changes so Back is a real undo.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:148-153 (init reads the hash once) and app.js:111-115 (history.replaceState)

fixes.title: Rebuild the segment palette so adjacent wedges differ in lightness, not just hue
fixes.rationale: Measured adjacent-pair contrast across the six WHEEL_COLORS: 1.06, 1.04, 1.13, 1.20, 1.26 and 1.47:1 — every wedge is essentially the same lightness, separated only by a 2px 35%-white stroke. On Maren's washed-out wall panel with room lights on, and for the roughly 8% of boys in any classroom with red-green deficiency, the wheel reads as one mid-tone blur. The research's colorRecommendation is explicit: 'build the segment ramp by index-with-stride so adjacent wedges always differ in both hue and lightness'. Label contrast is already fine (5.02:1 to 7.58:1 white-on-fill) so keep white labels and vary the fills' luminance instead.

fixes.title: Add a session result log — the fairness receipt
fixes.rationale: Devon's chat is primed to shout 'rigged' and he has nothing to point at: #winner is overwritten on the next spin (app.js:81) and no history is kept. The mechanics are actually clean — 20,000 simulated spins deviated at most 4.9% from even, and the pixel under the pointer matched the announced winner 4/4 — but the app keeps no evidence of it. The research documents live rigging suspicion (r/AskPC, r/UnethicalLifeProTips) and notes competitors already market 'CSPRNG' and 'provably random' as purchase criteria. Fix: an ordered, timestamped list of results below the wheel, copyable as plain text, plus switching Math.random (app.js:82-83) to crypto.getRandomValues so the claim can honestly be made in the copy.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/app.js:81 and 96-98 (winner assignment); randomness at app.js:82-83

fixes.title: Make print produce a roster, not a wheel and three dead buttons
fixes.rationale: Verified under emulateMedia({media:'print'}) with 28 names: header and footer correctly hidden, but #spinBtn still prints as inline-flex, the three action buttons print, the .hint prints, the full-colour 380px canvas prints, and #names renders at 104px against a scrollHeight of 718px — about 4 of 28 names reach the paper and the rest are clipped away invisibly. The research names 'degrade gracefully to paper' as a differentiator and specifically asks for cut-up slips and a numbered roster: 'the move that says we understand the popsicle-stick user'. Fix: add #spinBtn, .row and #wheel to the existing noprint set, and render the entry list as a real numbered <ol> (plus an optional cut-slips grid) for print.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/index.html:1197 (the print display:none list) and the @media print block starting index.html:1181

fixes.title: Fix the two hardcoded colours that escape the token system
fixes.rationale: Sampled in dark mode: the QR dialog computes a rgb(18,18,18) background while its heading is rgb(17,17,17) from an inline style="color:#111" — roughly 1.0:1, so 'Scan to open this wheel' is invisible and the dialog reads as broken. And the wheel hub is ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff', sampled rgb(255,255,255) — a bright white disc at the centre of the wheel in Devon's dark room. Everything else in the app themes correctly (body rgb(27,17,21), --chip #30242a, the empty disc correctly samples rgba(48,36,42,255)), which makes these two stand out as oversights rather than choices.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/index.html:1314 (h3 inline color:#111) and apps/wheel-picker/app.js:70-73 (hub fillStyle)

fixes.title: Raise the removal checkbox to a 44px target and enlarge the empty state
fixes.rationale: smallTargets() reports #removeMode at 13x20px on every viewport tested, and only 13x30 even at Largest text — under the 44px comfort floor. Bea's tremor made it a miss every time; Priya is one-handed with a clipboard. The wrapping label.chk does work as a hit area, which keeps this minor rather than major. Separately the empty state — the very first thing a new user sees — is canvas text drawn at 28px on the 760px backing canvas, which is 12.5 CSS px on a phone, the smallest text on the page; Bea did not see it and asked what to do.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/index.html:1298 (input#removeMode) and index.html:1266 (label.chk); empty state at apps/wheel-picker/app.js:40-42

fixes.title: Render the skip link the stylesheet already pays for
fixes.rationale: The .skip component is fully styled at index.html:840-849 and correctly excluded from print at 1196, and <main id="main"> exists at index.html:1280, but no skip element is ever rendered — verified by tabbing, where the first stop is #swsPrefsBtn. The cost is one line of markup for a component that is already built, and it matters more here than in most apps because keyboard users currently re-traverse the document after every spin.
fixes.where: apps/wheel-picker/index.html:1272 (before header.app; component styled at 840, target at 1280)

audit.purpose: A canvas spinning wheel for picking a name at random. Paste names into one textarea, press SPIN, watch a 4.2s eased rotation, read the winner. Optional 'remove the winner after each spin' for classroom/raffle elimination. There is no backend and no localStorage: the entire wheel state (names + removeMode) is base64url-encoded into the URL hash, so the link IS the save file, and it can be copied or shown as a QR code.
audit.structure: Single short page, no scrolling nav, one dialog. body > div.wrap containing: (1) header.app — 32px icon.svg alt="" (index.html:1274), h1 "Wheel Picker" (1275), span.spacer (1276), a#tipLink.tipbtn.hidden un-hidden by JS (1277); sws-prefs.js injects button#swsPrefsBtn immediately before the tip link at runtime. (2) main#main (1280) holding two section.card. Card 1 (1282-1289): div.wheelwrap > div.pointer[aria-hidden] (1284) + canvas#wheel width=760 height=760 aria-label="Spinning wheel of names" (1285); div#winner[aria-live=assertive] (1287); button#spinBtn.btn.primary.big with inline style="width:100%" (1288). Card 1 has NO h2 and no accessible name. Card 2 (1291-1306): h2 "Who's on the wheel" (1292) rendered by the base as a 12px uppercase micro-label; textarea#names with a four-line placeholder (1293-1297); label.chk wrapping input#removeMode[type=checkbox] with inline style="width:auto" (1298-1299); div.row with three equal .btn — #shareBtn, #qrBtn, #resetBtn (1300-1304); p.hint carrying the privacy/permanence promise (1305). Outside .wrap: div#toast[role=status][aria-live=polite] (1310), footer.colophon with two links carrying inline style="color:inherit" (1311), and dialog#qrDlg (1313-1317) with an inline-styled h3, canvas#qrCanvas 300x300 and button#qrClose. Scripts: sws-prefs.js classic blocking in head (1268), sws-ui.js classic (1269), vendor-qrcode.js classic exposing global qrcode() (1318), app.js as a module (1319). There is NO skip link element (the .skip component is styled at 840 but never rendered), NO <noscript>, NO empty-state markup, and NO hero block. Flow: init() (app.js:141) wires events, reveals the tip link, decodes location.hash once into the textarea, calls draw(), and registers sw.js. Every keystroke in #names re-parses, clears the removal buffer, rewrites the hash via history.replaceState and repaints the canvas — no debounce (measured 2.59ms per redraw at 100 names, so none is needed).

#winner — APP LAYER: centred, font-size 1.5rem, font-weight 800, min-height 2.2rem, overflow-wrap:anywhere (1260-1263); the 24px reveal
label.chk — APP LAYER: flex row, gap 8px, font-size .9rem (a raw rem, not a token), colour var(--muted) (1266)
#swsPrefs and its .opt / .sws-sample / .sws-note internals — the comfort dialog, styled in the base and built at runtime by sws-prefs.js
audit.dynamicMarkup: Almost nothing is injected — this app's runtime work is canvas painting, not DOM building. (1) sws-prefs.js creates button#swsPrefsBtn and inserts it immediately before .tipbtn inside header.app, then lazily builds dialog#swsPrefs on first click with seven radio groups (theme, text, density, reading, warmth, contrast, motion), a live type sample, Reset and Done. (2) app.js sets #tipLink.href and removes .hidden (app.js:143-147). (3) app.js writes #names.value from the decoded hash at init (152) and again after each removal (102) and restore (134). (4) #winner.textContent is set to '🎉 ' + winner at app.js:98 and cleared at 81 — textContent only, which is why '<script>alert(1)</script>' as a name is inert. (5) #toast.textContent plus a .show class, on a 2.4s timer (app.js:10-16). (6) canvas#wheel is fully repainted by draw() (app.js:31-74) on every keystroke and on every animation frame of a spin: wedges via sliceColor, a 2px rgba(255,255,255,.35) stroke, right-aligned rotated white labels truncated to 16 chars (10 above 24 names) at min(34, max(14, 320/n))px, and a hardcoded #ffffff 26px hub. The empty state is canvas text, '28px system-ui' reading 'Add names below' (app.js:40-42) — 12.5 CSS px as displayed. (7) canvas#qrCanvas is painted by showQr (app.js:162-177) from the global qrcode(); on throw it toasts and leaves the canvas blank. (8) history.replaceState rewrites the hash on every input, on removeMode change, on removal, on restore and before each share (app.js:111-115). Nothing is ever written to localStorage by this app — storage() measured 0 bytes after every scenario.

comfortDefects.issue: The comfort panel cannot touch the app's central object. With text set to Largest, body goes 16 -> 24px and #winner 24 -> 36px, but the canvas stays 340px wide and the on-wheel label size is unchanged, because it is computed from name count alone.
comfortDefects.where: app.js:65 (const fs = Math.min(34, Math.max(14, 320 / Math.max(n, 6)))) and app.js:63 (maxLen)
comfortDefects.fix: Scale the canvas font from the canvas's displayed width and the resolved root font size, so data-text feeds through; drop labels and switch to numbered wedges with a legend above the legible threshold.

comfortDefects.issue: Motion preference ignored. data-motion="less" and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce both produce the same measured 4,273ms rotation as the default.
comfortDefects.fix: Branch on the media query and the data-motion attribute to a non-rotating shuffle-and-settle reveal; expose a spin-length control.

comfortDefects.issue: The winner reveal never grows with the viewport — 24px measured at 320px, 414px and 1280px alike; 36px at Largest.
comfortDefects.fix: clamp(2rem, 9vw, 9rem), held as a full-bleed card until dismissed.

comfortDefects.issue: The wheel is capped at 380px on any screen, so a 1280px projector shows a phone-sized disc surrounded by empty card.
comfortDefects.fix: min(90vw, 70vh) above a tablet breakpoint, plus a chrome-free presentation mode.

comfortDefects.issue: input#removeMode is a 13x20px hit target (13x30 even at Largest text), under the 44px floor. The wrapping label.chk does provide a larger effective target, which limits the damage.
comfortDefects.fix: Give the input min-width/min-height 24px with padding on the label to reach a 44px row, or use the .chip.on toggle pattern already in the stylesheet.

comfortDefects.issue: Adjacent wedge colours are all the same lightness — measured pairwise contrast 1.04:1 to 1.47:1 — so the wheel reads as one mid-tone blur on a washed-out projector and for red-green colourblind viewers. Label contrast itself is fine (5.02:1 to 7.58:1 white-on-fill).
comfortDefects.fix: A ramp that varies lightness as well as hue, assigned by stride so neighbours never match.

comfortDefects.issue: The empty state — the first thing any new user sees — is canvas text at 28px on the 760px backing canvas, which is 12.5 CSS px as displayed, the smallest text on the page. The .empty component that would do this properly is styled and unused.
comfortDefects.fix: Render a real .empty block over/under the canvas: glyph, 'Nobody on the wheel yet', 'Paste your list below — one name per line'.

comfortDefects.issue: The wheel hub is hardcoded #ffffff, sampled rgb(255,255,255) in dark mode — a bright white disc in a dark room.
comfortDefects.fix: Read --surface (or --chip) from the computed body style as the empty-state path already does at app.js:37.

comfortDefects.issue: The QR dialog heading is invisible in dark mode: computed rgb(17,17,17) on a rgb(18,18,18) dialog, roughly 1.0:1.
comfortDefects.fix: Drop the inline colour and let the dialog inherit --ink; give #qrDlg an explicit --surface background.

comfortDefects.issue: label.chk sets font-size:.9rem as a raw value rather than a token, so the removal toggle's label sits outside the type scale (it still scales with root size, so this is consistency rather than breakage).

#spinBtn stays 52px tall at every text size — measured unchanged from Default through Largest — while its label text grows, so the button gets visually tighter exactly when a user has asked for more room.
comfortDefects.fix: Express the big-button height in em or add a data-text-aware min-height.

comfortDefects.issue: No spin-speed control of any kind exists — a /speed|duration|fast/ scan of the rendered page finds nothing — so the 4.2s animation is mandatory for everyone.
comfortDefects.fix: A three-stop speed control beside the removal toggle, persisted with the other prefs.

navigationDefects.issue: Elimination dead-ends one short: with one name left, SPIN refuses with 'Add at least two names' and the last person is never picked or announced.
navigationDefects.fix: Allow a final spin that lands on and announces the sole remaining entry, then offer 'Reset for next period'.

navigationDefects.issue: 'Restore removed names' is disarmed by any keystroke — the input handler clears the removal buffer, so editing the list mid-period silently destroys the undo. Verified: it then reports 'Nobody has been removed yet'.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:121 (removed = [] inside the #names input handler); button at index.html:1303
navigationDefects.fix: Reconcile the edit against the removed set instead of discarding it; model picked-ness as a flag on one list.

navigationDefects.issue: Restore reorders the list — names.concat(removed) turns an alphabetical A,B,C register into B|A|C.
navigationDefects.fix: Restore in original position, which falls out for free from the single-list-with-flags model.

navigationDefects.issue: No hashchange listener. Pasting a shared wheel link into an already-open tab changes the URL and nothing else — verified, the textarea kept its old contents. This is the app's only persistence mechanism.
navigationDefects.fix: addEventListener('hashchange', …) that re-decodes, ignoring the app's own replaceState writes.

navigationDefects.issue: Back desynchronises the URL from the wheel. syncHash uses history.replaceState, so Back jumps to a stale encoded state without re-initialising: the address bar showed one wheel and the textarea another.
navigationDefects.fix: pushState on meaningful changes plus the hashchange listener, making Back a real undo.

navigationDefects.issue: No count anywhere. No entry count, no 'X of 28 left' during elimination, no notice when the 100-name cap or the 40-char truncation fires — verified, no /\d+\s+names?/ text exists in the DOM at any list size.
navigationDefects.fix: A live count beside the h2 at index.html:1292 and a remaining-count beside the removal toggle.

navigationDefects.issue: No dedupe affordance: four identical 'Sam' entries produce four slices with no notice, and the DOM contains no 'duplicate' text.
navigationDefects.where: helpers.js:3-7 (parseNames trims and filters but never dedupes)
navigationDefects.fix: Dedupe with an undoable toast — SWS.undo from the now-loaded sws-ui.js is exactly this.

navigationDefects.issue: The share link outgrows the QR silently: at 100 forty-char names the URL is 5,788 chars, qrcode() throws, and the user gets 'Could not draw the QR' with no cause, no cure and a blank canvas.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:162-177 (showQr, catch at 174); button at index.html:1302
navigationDefects.fix: Check payload length first and say what to do instead; consider compressing the payload.

navigationDefects.issue: There is no saved-wheel concept at all — no named wheels, no list, no export, no import. storage() is 0 bytes; the only save is a bookmark of a hash URL.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:111-115 is the entire persistence layer; UI space at index.html:1300-1304
navigationDefects.fix: Autosave to localStorage, a named-wheel list with rename/duplicate/delete, and Export all / Import.

navigationDefects.issue: Card 1 — the wheel, the winner and the primary action — has no h2 and therefore no accessible name, so a screen-reader user landmark-hopping gets an unnamed region containing the whole product.
navigationDefects.fix: Add an h2 (visually the micro-label style is unobtrusive) or aria-label the section.

navigationDefects.issue: No result history — #winner is overwritten on the next spin and nothing is retained, so there is no fairness receipt for chat or the staffroom and no record of who has already been picked once removal mode is off.
navigationDefects.fix: An ordered timestamped log below the wheel, copyable as plain text.

navigationDefects.issue: The privacy/permanence promise is a 13px .hint at the bottom of the second card, below the fold on a phone, and the .trust banner component that exists for exactly this is unused. The research calls the IT-approval sentence this app's single most defensible differentiator.
navigationDefects.fix: A .trust line at the top of main: 'Names you type stay in this browser. Nothing is uploaded, no account, no analytics.'

a11yDefects.issue: The primary action destroys keyboard focus. Setting spinBtn.disabled while it holds focus moves activeElement to <body> — verified still <body> after the spin completes and the button is re-enabled — so a second Space does nothing and every subsequent spin needs three Tabs from the top of the document. axe does not detect this (zero violations on load, after a spin, and with the prefs dialog open).
a11yDefects.fix: Keep the button focusable and guard on the existing `spinning` flag; use aria-disabled plus aria-busy, and move focus to the result when it lands.

a11yDefects.issue: No skip link is rendered, though the .skip component is fully styled and print-hidden and <main id="main"> exists as its target. First Tab lands on the comfort-settings button.
a11yDefects.where: component at index.html:840-849, print rule at 1196, target at 1280, no element anywhere
a11yDefects.fix: Skip to the wheel as the first child of body.

a11yDefects.issue: '🎉 undefined' can be announced into an aria-live=assertive region: clearing the textarea mid-spin makes sliceAtPointer return -1 and names[-1] is undefined.
a11yDefects.fix: Snapshot the entry list at spin start and bail cleanly if it is empty.

a11yDefects.issue: The winner announcement leads with an emoji, so screen readers say 'party popper' before the name in an assertive interruption.
a11yDefects.fix: Put the emoji in an aria-hidden span and keep the live region's text to 'Winner: <name>'.

a11yDefects.issue: canvas#wheel carries only aria-label="Spinning wheel of names" and no fallback content, so the wheel's contents are unavailable to assistive tech. It is partially rescued by the textarea holding the same list, but the wheel never states how many entries it has or which are already picked.
a11yDefects.fix: role="img" with an aria-label that is regenerated on draw ('Wheel with 28 names, 12 already picked'), or an adjacent visually-hidden list.

a11yDefects.issue: Nothing announces that the spin has started. #spinBtn simply goes disabled for 4.2 seconds with no aria-busy and no polite status, so a screen-reader user gets silence and then an assertive result.
a11yDefects.fix: aria-busy on the wheel region plus a polite 'Spinning…' status.

a11yDefects.issue: The removal toggle's outcome is not announced. When a winner is removed the textarea is rewritten and the wheel redrawn 900ms later with no status message.
a11yDefects.fix: A polite toast, 'Marcus removed — 27 left', which doubles as the counter the research asks for.

a11yDefects.issue: input#removeMode is a 13x20px target, under the 44px floor at every viewport and preference combination tested.
a11yDefects.fix: Pad the label to a 44px row and enlarge the control.

a11yDefects.issue: Card 1 is an unnamed <section>, so its implicit region landmark has no accessible name.

The QR dialog's heading is unreadable in dark mode (rgb(17,17,17) on rgb(18,18,18)) — a 1.0:1 contrast failure that axe misses because the colour comes from an inline style on a dialog that is closed at scan time.
a11yDefects.fix: Remove the inline colour; theme the dialog with tokens.

a11yDefects.issue: No <noscript>. With modules blocked the page renders a header, an empty canvas, a dead SPIN button and a textarea that does nothing.
a11yDefects.fix: A <noscript> line explaining that the wheel needs JavaScript.

a11yDefects.issue: The 4.2-second rotation ignores both prefers-reduced-motion and the app's own Motion=Reduced setting — the clearest WCAG 2.3.3 / vestibular-safety gap in the app, and the one the research singles out as the category's blind spot.

audit.printSupport: Partial and misleading. The shared print block (index.html:1181-1235) correctly hides header.app, footer.colophon, .tipbtn, #toast, .skip, #swsPrefsBtn and #swsPrefs (1196-1197), forces black text and flattens borders and shadows. But this app adds nothing of its own, so under emulateMedia({media:'print'}) with 28 names loaded the paper gets: the full-colour 380px canvas wheel (display:block), #spinBtn still inline-flex, all three action buttons in .row still flex, the .hint paragraph, and — the real failure — textarea#names rendered at 104px against a scrollHeight of 718px, which puts roughly 4 of 28 names on the page and clips the other 24 away with nothing to indicate they exist. There is no printable roster and no cut-slips output, which the research names as a differentiator ('degrade gracefully to paper... the move that says we understand the popsicle-stick user'). Minimum fix: add #spinBtn, .row and #wheel to the noprint set and render the entries as a numbered <ol> for print.
riskyToRestyle: canvas#wheel's width/height attributes are the drawing buffer, not the display size, and app.js caches CX, CY and R from them at module load (app.js:29) — before any layout runs. Changing width="760" height="760" at index.html:1285 changes the coordinate space every draw call assumes. Restyle the CSS width only (#wheel{width:100%;height:auto} at index.html:1252); never touch the attributes without also touching app.js:29.

Every on-wheel dimension is a magic number in canvas units, not CSS: R = width/2 - 8, the 26px hub radius, the label baseline at R - 18 and fs/3, the 2px stroke (app.js:29, 67, 71). They only look right at a 760px buffer. Changing the buffer or the aspect ratio silently misplaces all of them.

.wheelwrap{max-width:380px} (index.html:1253) is load-bearing for the pointer: div.pointer is absolutely positioned at top:-6px, left:50% of .wheelwrap (1255-1259), so it only sits on the wheel's rim while the wrapper's width equals the canvas's displayed width. Any padding, border or non-100% canvas width detaches the pointer from the disc.

The pointer is a CSS border triangle using border-top:22px solid var(--ink). Give .pointer a background, a border-radius or a different border-width and it stops being a triangle. It is also the only element that must read as 'on top of' the wheel, and it relies on z-index:2 against a canvas with no stacking context of its own.

#winner has min-height:2.2rem (index.html:1260) precisely so the layout does not jump when a winner appears; the wheel and SPIN button would shift by a line otherwise. Removing it to 'tidy up' introduces a 4.2-second-delayed layout shift under the user's finger.

Slice fill colours are hardcoded hex in helpers.js:43 and are the only colours in the app that do not come from tokens — but they are also what the white labels' 5.02:1 to 7.58:1 contrast depends on. Swapping them for token values without re-checking label contrast will break legibility. The sliceColor wrap-around special case (helpers.js:48) assumes exactly six colours; change the array length and that guard is wrong.

The empty state reads getComputedStyle(document.body) for --chip and color on every draw (app.js:37-39). It is the one canvas path that is theme-aware, so it will follow token renames — while the hub's #ffffff and the labels' #ffffff will not. Rename tokens and the disc changes colour while the hub does not.

dialog#qrDlg carries its layout in an inline style attribute (index.html:1313) and its heading colour in another (1314). A stylesheet rule for dialog will lose to both. Restyling the QR dialog means editing the markup, not the CSS.
#spinBtn carries inline style="width:100%" (index.html:1288), which beats any .btn width rule. Anything that tries to place SPIN in a row with other controls has to remove that attribute first.

#names is a plain textarea with base styling only (index.html:505) and its content IS the data model — app.js writes to .value on load, removal and restore. Replacing it with a chip/list UI is not a restyle; it rewrites the persistence path (app.js:102, 121, 134, 152).

app.js:104 redraws the wheel on a bare setTimeout(draw, 900) after a removal, deliberately leaving the winner's slice on screen for most of a second. Any change that makes draw() dependent on freshly measured layout will run inside that orphan timer with no guarantee the element is still in its previous state.

The app declares its own module-scoped toast() (app.js:9-16) while sws-ui.js now loads and exposes window.SWS.toast/undo. Both target the same #toast element (index.html:1310). Migrating to SWS.toast is worth doing for the undo affordances, but doing it halfway means two owners of one node and two competing dismiss timers.
